answer: Sequential Dependency Chain. Each new agent identity must submit a cipher challenge whose solution depends on the prior block's output, so identities can only be created in series, never in parallel. A glacier of precomputed identities gains nothing because the chain advances one link per wall-clock interval. The kernel enforces this by rejecting any registration that skips the current chain head. Attacker cost: one full serialization delay plus compute per identity, making mass creation linear in time rather than free.
